comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C74-C76, C172-C176 regarding the V149Q docking-deficient mutant. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find this experimental design and the conclusion that high-FRET state is distinct from docking to be well-supported.

Strong agreement on claims C46-C48, C65, C127 regarding FRET-compatible mutant design and validation. Both evaluations accept the functional characterization without critique, though OpenEval also addresses C128 which peer review does not explicitly mention.

Both support claims C129-C136 regarding ionic strength effects on SBD interactions from smFRET data. OpenEval also includes C137 in this evaluation. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the quality and convincing nature of these findings.

Both support claims C149-C154 regarding glycine betaine effects and conformational sensitivity. OpenEval evaluates these as part of ligand-dependent behavior (C146-C154), while peer review groups them with broader smFRET findings on transient SBD interactions.

Both support the cryo-EM data (claims C161-C162, C165-C169, C171). OpenEval finds the modest resolution appropriate for flexible domains, and peer reviewers accept the low-resolution data as corroborating smFRET findings despite limitations.

Both support claims C61-C64 regarding methodological improvements and sample quality. OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of SEC profiles and monodispersity (C49-C64), while peer review implicitly accepts sample preparation quality through praise of method application.

Both support claims C68, C70 regarding identification of two FRET states with sub-millisecond dynamics. OpenEval emphasizes burst variance analysis and mpH2MM modeling (C66-C70), while peer review groups these with broader smFRET findings.

Both support claims C83, C87-C88 regarding persistence of high-FRET state and weak interactions. OpenEval provides detailed evaluation including geometric calculations (C83-C88, C138-C145), while peer review accepts these as part of the overall smFRET evidence.

Significant disagreement on claims C113-C117, C120-C121 regarding the main mechanistic conclusion. OpenEval finds the proposed mechanism well-supported, while peer reviewers rate it as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is inferred by exclusion rather than direct demonstration.

Disagreement on claims C102-C105 regarding the sideways interaction model. OpenEval finds the model supported by multiple lines of evidence (C90, C95-C106), while peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting alternative models are excluded rather than the proposed model being directly demonstrated.

Both rate claims C107-C108 as speculative/uncertain regarding quinary structure interpretation. OpenEval notes this is plausible but would benefit from additional validation, while peer reviewers question whether the model is directly supported by experimental data.

Disagreement on claims C118-C119 regarding connection to cooperativity. OpenEval finds the explanation for previous cooperativity observations well-supported, while peer reviewers note the relation to cooperativity remains unclear and insufficiently demonstrated.

Both address claims C90, C106 but with different emphases. OpenEval evaluates the sideways interaction model as supported (C90, C95-C106), while peer review focuses on cryo-EM data (C106, C161-C171) as corroborating evidence without specifically evaluating the interaction model.

OpenEval evaluates claims C77-C82 regarding FRET shifts not representing docking, finding this interpretation reasonable based on inconsistent behavior across variants. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval rates claims C122-C126 as UNCERTAIN, noting broader implications about prevalence and periplasmic concentrations are reasonable hypotheses but not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
Peer review explicitly evaluates claim C7 (part of broader smFRET findings) as supported, but this claim is not addressed in any OpenEval result.
Peer review evaluates claims C9, C51, C89 as part of cryo-EM support, but these specific claims are not addressed in OpenEval results (though overlapping claims are covered).
Peer review evaluates claims C10 as part of the uncertain mechanistic model, but this specific claim is not addressed in any OpenEval result.
Peer review evaluates claims C37-C38 regarding previous cooperativity observations as uncertain in their mechanistic connection, but these claims are not addressed in OpenEval results.
